# How Lockheed Martin is organized: four segments, one customer that matters most

Defense News, March 3, 2026

Lockheed Martin, the Bethesda, Maryland-based contractor formed by the 1995 merger of Lockheed Corporation and Martin Marietta, reports through four business segments: Aeronautics, Missiles and Fire Control, Rotary and Mission Systems, and Space. The company employed roughly 121,000 people at the end of 2025, according to its annual report.

Aeronautics, anchored by the F-35 program, remains the largest segment by revenue. Missiles and Fire Control has been the fastest-growing segment as PAC-3 and GMLRS demand from the U.S. Army and allied customers outpaces production. Rotary and Mission Systems houses Sikorsky helicopters and the Aegis combat system, while Space builds satellites and the Trident II D5 ballistic missile.

Roughly three quarters of sales come from the U.S. government, a concentration the company's own filings flag as a risk and that distinguishes it from more commercially exposed peers such as Boeing and RTX.
